title: Azure VM Manager
summary: A guarded operations platform for Azure virtual machines, designed around visibility, simulation, approvals, audit evidence, and safe execution.
evidence: Sealed version 1 after 71 roadmap items, then added backend-enforced approval gates, controlled bulk power actions, an executable patch runbook, and Azure Policy compliance integration. Verification included 71 backend and 59 frontend tests.

title: Patch Compliance & Recovery Automation
summary: Reusable Windows Server patch assessment and pre-change recovery workflows for managed environments.
evidence: Validated Server 2016–2025 security baselines, separated unreachable from non-compliant systems, and produced console, CSV, and HTML evidence. A companion Azure workflow prepared snapshots for 12 VMs with WhatIf, duplicate detection, and readiness gates.

title: KnowledgeForge
summary: A governed pipeline for converting years of technical conversations into durable, publishable knowledge without losing provenance or human control.
evidence: Established immutable source retention, checksum-bound intake, privacy review, verification gates, approval-controlled publication, and a bounded real-export pilot. Milestone 1 and 2 exit assessments passed before advancing classification work.

title: Infrastructure Evidence Toolkit
summary: A collection of investigation and inventory tools built for repeatable diagnosis across enterprise Windows environments.
evidence: Created reusable workflows for WinRM discovery, WSUS exposure, archived security events, Active Directory, hypervisors, and detailed reboot-event capture—each designed to distinguish verified findings from assumptions.

title: CharterOS V2
summary: A clean-room architecture and controlled delivery plan for a second-generation charter operations platform.
evidence: Completed the M0 architecture and evidence boundary, documented a Proxmox-backed Compose staging model, threat model, domain contracts, synthetic golden journeys, and a gated first slice. Live data, payment, messaging, and provider integrations remain explicitly blocked.

title: Front Range Insurance Lab
summary: A bilingual reference experience and reusable deployment starter for independent insurance agencies.
evidence: Built adaptive intake, English and Spanish journeys, secure handoff boundaries, portable standalone Node output, Docker/VPS packaging, and AMD64 CI coverage. The fictional reference agency remains private and clearly labeled as concept mode.
